rules.statement: Every `uses:` in a GitHub Actions workflow names the full commit SHA of the action's release, with the version in a trailing comment (e.g. `actions/setup-dotnet@<sha> # v6.0.0`), never a mutable tag such as `@v6`.
rules.why: A retagged or compromised tag would run new code in jobs that may hold publish credentials; SHA pins are immutable and Dependabot moves them.
rules.check: Look for `uses: owner/action@vN` or any branch or tag reference in added or changed workflow steps instead of a 40-character SHA with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment.

rules.statement: Don't report a workflow step's `working-directory: .` as redundant until you have checked whether the job sets `defaults.run.working-directory`, because the step may need the override to run a script at the repository root.
rules.why: When a job sets a default working directory, the step's explicit `.` is what makes a root-level script resolve, just as its neighbouring steps rely on it.
rules.check: Before reporting, read the job's `defaults.run.working-directory` and where the step's script lives.

rules.statement: Don't ask a project built from the project template to move workflow blocks the template generates into a project-local composite action; the deduplication belongs upstream in the template.
rules.why: A project-side refactor of template-generated blocks would drift from what every template update merges.
rules.check: Before suggesting you deduplicate repeated workflow steps, check whether the project template generates them (e.g. in ci.yml or copilot-setup-steps.yml). If it does, point the change upstream.

rules.statement: Don't object to a changelog or catalog entry that links the issues it comes from, even issues that track template-alignment work rather than a product capability, because the project-template convention has a catalog entry link the issues behind it.
rules.why: Project-template ADR-0015 says a catalog entry links the issues behind it, and those links stay accurate once the issues close.
rules.check: Before reporting issue links in a CHANGELOG entry, check whether the linked issues are what the entry comes from.
